The next step is to break each integer into a prefix of log m = 3 bits, and a suffix of log n − log m =
log(n/m) = 2 bits. The suffixes form the first component EF1 of the EF data structure:
x ∈ S prefix of(x)2 EF1 = suffix of(x)2
Note that the suffixes use in total mlog(n/m) bits. We store EF1 = (00,01,00,00,10,01,00,11)
with the packed array data structure of Theorem 1.3.9. As far as the prefixes are concerned, observe
that they form a list of m nondecreasing integers of log m bits each. We will store the differences
between consecutive integers in the list, in unary encoding: difference δi = pi − pi−1, where pi is the
i-th prefix, is encoded as 0δi1 (i.e. δi occurrences of bit ’0’ followed by one bit ’1’). For example, the
difference δ8 between the two adjacent prefixes p7 = 101 and p8 = 111 is (111 − 101)2 = 2; we encode
this difference as δ8 = 021 = 001. The first difference is defined as δ1 = p1. The concatenated bits of
this encoding of δ1,...,δm is the second part EF2 of the EF data structure:
